Building 06-CP-65 (State Historic Preservation Office [SHPO] Resource # B18910) is a contributing element to the Area 6 Control Point Historic District (SHPO Resource # D395), which has been determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) under Criteria A and C (O’Neill et al. 2021; Reed 2022). The scope of work for the undertaking includes installing a new felt-backed PVC membrane that is white in color and two new heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) units on the roof. To properly repair the leaks and install the membrane, all existing equipment will be dismantled and removed from the roof. The existing equipment is highly visible, dates from the period of significance for the historic property and is character-defining (see Figure 3). Therefore, its removal constitutes an adverse effect. MITIGATION FOR BUILDING 06-CP-65 The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), National Nuclear Security Administration Nevada Field Office (NNSA/NFO), in consultation with the SHPO and the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP), defined standard mitigation for undertakings adversely affecting contributing elements in historic districts in NNSS PA Appendix D. NNSA/NFO notified the SHPO of its intention to utilize the standard mitigation via letter dated April 8, 2025 (Julian to Reed) and the ACHP via their e106 filing system. The SHPO agreed to the use of standard mitigation as defined in the NNSS PA in a letter dated July 8, 2025 (Krupicz to Julian). Appendix D.I outlines standard mitigation for contributing elements in historic districts, such as Building 06-CP-65. The mitigation consists of an updated Architectural Resource Assessment (ARA) form to document current conditions (Appendix D.I.A), including high-quality digital images (Appendix D.I.A.1) and plans, drawings, or annotated sketch plans (Appendix D.I.A.2), and a brief letter report describing mitigation contents and summarizing the building’s historic significance (Appendix D.I.B). This mitigation report documents the completion of mitigation for Building 06-CP-65 in accordance with NNSS PA Appendix D. An ARA Update form was prepared to satisfy NNSS PA Appendix D.I.A (see Attachment A). It provides additional information about the historic property, an individual NRHP evaluation, and interior description, engineering drawings, and current photographs. This letter report fulfills NNSS PA Appendix D.I.B. DESCRIPTION OF BUILDING 06-CP-65 Building 06-CP-65 was constructed in 1966 as a large warehouse for equipment used in the forward areas of the NNSS (see Figures 1-3). It also contained office space for engineers, administrative functions, and laboratories. Referred to as the Technical Support Building, it is one in a number of large, utilitarian concrete buildings that comprise the Area 6 Control Point Historic District. Because it was constructed after the 1963 Limited Test Ban Treaty, the warehouse and the equipment that it housed would have been related to underground tests (as opposed to earlier atmospheric tests) that took place at various locations in the forward areas of the NNSS.
